title: Germany, 1923
notes: All stills; every one is a large scan, so each push travels into a detail. Moves are in frame fractions of the fitted 1920×1080 picture (as preview.py reads them).

Banknotes rise in order: 500 million (P2.04), then three hard cuts 10 billion → 20 billion → 500 billion across '…anyway. / More notes. / Fewer goods.' The edit plan listed them 10 bn → 500 bn → 20 bn, which would make the numbers fall on the last cut; re-ordered so they only climb.

The storyboard/plan give P2.06 'The state pays the workers anyway' no picture of its own; it opens on 'French at Essen' (troops with a machine gun outside the 'Commerz- und Privat-Bank') for 1.8 s, then the first of the three notes lands under 'anyway'.

P2.09 'The currency collapses' holds on 'Gov't notice of French Invasion at Essen' as the plan says. Its subject is the invasion notice, not the currency; it reads as a crowd reading bad news. Alternative: hold the Berlin Bank stacks again.

lines.json puts P9.09 ('So.', a Part 9 line) at 124.53–125.0 inside this scene. That is almost certainly a lines.py mis-match on a repeated word; no clip is anchored to it (the bread-crowd clip runs from P2.08 across it). If retime.py maps P9.09 to its real place in scene 12–14, the time map inside this scene will be wrong: fix lines.json first.
gov.archives.arc.88967 (International News 442, 1921) is not in the conform status, and its only relevant item is Pershing at Coblenz in 1921: not used.
The verb card sits across 'That is one thing you can do with a money tree. You can shake it.' (5 s).
